126  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

Their union has been blessed with three children: Moses, whose name introduces this record; Wyatt and Lester. The father has given all his time and attention to his education in Fort Worth and Gainesville, Texas. He is at present with his parents, a prominent and popular young man of Davis. The daughter was educated in Savoy College and is now Mrs. Pearl (Moses) Pierce, of the town of Davis.

Moses Chipley, whose name introduces this record, was educated in Savoy College and at Franklin, Tennessee. He is a prominent lawyer, and is interested with all questions of general interest. His attention is given to the stock-raising in the Chickasaw Nation, and the attention of the press upon him makes him a very important pursuit. He, too, is a well known factor in political and commercial life, and represents his county in the legislature. He has held the office of County Attorney, and at one time was connected with Ivan Trading Company, Clerk of Territory.

RECEPTION OF INDIANS TO THE SAVOY COLLEGE TRAINING.

The interesting data just reported in the talk of ex-students of the College, the author received the assistance of Professor Holland. She wishes to express her considerable search made contact with a retired peace officer named Frank Anderson, a Chickasaw Indian, who was raised in his own town El Kena, was sent to the College in 1886 at the age of thirteen, before the Savoy public school closed. His retrospective appreciation of the college and the human ideals brought out in the sketch of this early boyhood training as given in his life sketch are here reproduced in photostat as a memorial to the college. The introduction was written by Mrs. Welborn of Paris, Texas, and Mr. Anderson himself.

Mr. Anderson:

Born in Tishomingo, Chickasaw Nation, Indian Territory, August 20th, 1877. I am a full-blood Choctaw Indian.
